_note: Transcription of the exact Railway Template Composer settings for the PostgreSQL 19 + pgvector template. Railway does NOT read this file automatically: enter these settings in the Template Composer when publishing, and check the published page against this file. The Postgres service builds from the GitHub repo's Dockerfile, which uses the pgvector project's official image (pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg19-trixie, pinned by digest): PostgreSQL 19.0 with pgvector 0.8.7 built in. The Backup service builds from services/backup/Dockerfile in the same repo.
category_note: Railway's category list has no 'Database' option (checked 2026-11-03); Storage is the closest available filing.
description: PostgreSQL 19 + pgvector, with SSL and scheduled backups
name: PostgreSQL 19 + pgvector
notIncluded: Point-in-time recovery (backups are scheduled pg_dump archives; a restore lands at backup time, not at an arbitrary moment)
Major-version auto upgrade (moving to a future major version is a dump and restore)

healthcheck.note: Database services have no HTTP healthcheck path. Health is proven by an authenticated psql connection (SELECT 1) plus a pgvector query, as in scripts/local-test.sh, not by process liveness alone.

source.note: Builds the repo Dockerfile (pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg19-trixie base, digest pinned).

tcpProxy.note: Enable the TCP proxy so users can connect from outside Railway; service-to-service traffic uses the private domain.

PGURL.note: Connection string for other services in the same project.

PG_SSL.note: on (default): the server presents a self-signed TLS certificate and accepts sslmode=require connections; off disables TLS. Plain connections keep working either way.

POSTGRES_INIT_DUMP_BASE64.note: Optional. A pg_dump SQL file (plain or gzipped), base64-encoded, applied once at first start on an empty data directory. Empty means no import.

POSTGRES_INIT_DUMP_URL.note: Optional. https URL of a .sql or .sql.gz pg_dump file, applied once at first start on an empty data directory. Empty means no import. Takes precedence over POSTGRES_INIT_DUMP_BASE64.

POSTGRES_PASSWORD.note: Generated at deploy time by the template secret() function. The alphabet is deliberately URL-safe (letters, digits, dash, underscore): the password is embedded in the PGURL and DATABASE_URL connection strings, and the earlier base64 alphabet could produce a '/' that breaks URI parsing in libpq (proven by the first live backup test, 2026-11-20, where pg_dump misread the port). Never a literal value.

DATABASE_URL.note: The standard connection string name, added 2026-11-23. Same value as PGURL. Apps, ORMs and tutorials expect DATABASE_URL; the template originally exposed only PGURL, which made the standard wiring find nothing.

DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL.note: Public connection string through the TCP proxy, for tools outside Railway. Mirrors the naming of Railway's own Postgres template.

volumes.note: Persistent volume. Since PostgreSQL 18 the official image keeps data in a major-version subdirectory (19/docker) under this mount; mounting at the old /var/lib/postgresql/data path makes the entrypoint refuse to start (proven by live test 2026-11-20). Without the volume, data is lost on redeploy. The TLS certificate also lives on this volume (certs/ next to the data directory).

source.note: Builds the backup image (same pinned postgres:19.0 base plus the AWS CLI) from the same repo.

BACKUP_RETENTION_COUNT.note: How many dumps to keep in the bucket; older ones are pruned after each run.

BUCKET_ACCESS_KEY_ID.note: Bucket credential, wired from the Backups bucket in the Composer (references as set 2026-11-20).

BUCKET_ENDPOINT.note: Bucket S3 endpoint, wired from the Backups bucket in the Composer.

BUCKET_NAME.note: Bucket name, wired from the Backups bucket in the Composer as ${{Backups.BUCKET}}: Railway's BUCKET variable is the globally unique S3 bucket name (display name plus a short hash). Do NOT use RAILWAY_BUCKET_NAME here: Railway's docs warn it is the display name, not the S3 API name, and wiring it made every upload fail with NoSuchBucket (proven live 2026-11-20 in test-pg19-f1).

BUCKET_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.note: Bucket credential, wired from the Backups bucket in the Composer.

DATABASE_URL.note: Private-network connection string for the Postgres service.

services.name: Backups
services.note: Railway Bucket (S3-compatible project storage) receiving the scheduled pg_dump archives under the pgdumps/ prefix.

stillUntestedAtPublish: Feature build LIVE VERIFIED 2026-11-20: TLS (TLS 1.3 over sslmode=require through the public proxy), first-boot dump import (imported table and row confirmed by query), and scheduled backups (repeated successful cron runs into the bucket, plus a passed restore drill: newest dump downloaded and pg_restore'd into a fresh database with the planted data and the vector extension working). Three live-found defects were fixed on the way: import connects over the local socket during init, the password generator uses a URL-safe alphabet, and BUCKET_NAME is wired from the bucket's BUCKET variable (the real S3 name), not RAILWAY_BUCKET_NAME (the display name). Not included and not claimed: point-in-time recovery and major-version auto upgrade.
